Thought: I need to determine which pair does not correctly represent an acid and its conjugate base. Let me analyze each option.

In an acid-base pair, the conjugate base is formed when the acid loses a proton (H+). So the conjugate base should have one less H+ than the acid.

A. H2SO4 and HSO4-
   H2SO4 loses one H+ to form HSO4-
   This is a correct acid-conjugate base pair.

B. H2SO4 and SO4^{2-}
   H2SO4 would need to lose two H+ to form SO4^{2-}
   This is not a direct acid-conjugate base pair because it involves losing two protons. The direct conjugate base of H2SO4 is HSO4-.

C. HNO3 and NO3-
   HNO3 loses one H+ to form NO3-
   This is a correct acid-conjugate base pair.

D. HSO4- and SO4^{2-}
   HSO4- loses one H+ to form SO4^{2-}
   This is a correct acid-conjugate base pair.

Looking at these options, B is incorrect because SO4^{2-} is not the direct conjugate base of H2SO4. The direct conjugate base of H2SO4 is HSO4-, and then HSO4- can further lose an H+ to form SO4^{2-}.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
